summary: A is materially closer to the frozen contract. It provides the exact Upload signature, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption usage, and tests multipart encoding, validation, reader errors, and retry behavior. B changes the required API and adds explicitly forbidden association machinery.
reasons: A implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly; B substitutes opts ...AddFileOption, breaking the mandated API.
A directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile as required. B introduces NewFileWithFields and deterministic-field machinery solely to support out-of-scope associations.
B adds WithFileDealID, WithFilePersonID, and other association options despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields.

A has stronger contract-focused tests: exact multipart field/name/content, FilesOption request propagation, validation, source-reader failure, Upload retry, and os.File retry body equality across both attempts. B omits an Upload source-reader-error test and does not verify Upload itself across a retry with streamed content or FilesOption compatibility.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data logic instead of routing the encoded body through Add, violating a central contract requirement.
The RawClient replayability change is an out-of-scope retry refactor and changes Add and all arbitrary reader requests by eagerly buffering them unless WithNoRetry is used.
The changelog and README advertise the broader buffering behavior, increasing the scope and compatibility implications of the patch.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong option type and changes established FilesOption behavior.
It adds expressly forbidden association fields and substantial duplicate option machinery.

Upload bypasses Add rather than centralizing request and error behavior there through the required route pattern or a suitable internal reuse mechanism compatible with Add semantics; it reimplements the request path directly like A does—violating the contract either way. More specifically, both candidates duplicate Add instead of calling it, but B also diverges from FilesOption entirely and expands multipart helper scope unnecessarily. Let me keep this risk concise: Upload duplicates Add rather than routing through it, so behavior can drift. (This string should ideally not self-correct.)
